Bucking choices and prices

Source: vignettes/bucking-prices.Rmd
bucking-prices.Rmd

merchandise() selects the longest eligible log within the reachable product sequence. optimize_bucking() selects cuts for value or net inside-bark cubic volume under the same specifications.

Optimize a tree 

## Select a shipped tree
tree <- example_trees %>%
  filter(tree == 5)
tree spcd species dbh ht model
5 202 Douglas-fir 20 100 F00FW2W202 
## Load the example specifications
specifications <- example_products(name = 'douglas_fir')
product lengths min_length max_length min_sed trim volume_unit
Large sawlog 32 NA NA 12 0.5 scribner
Medium sawlog 16 NA NA 10 0.5 scribner
Small sawlog 16 NA NA 6 0.5 scribner
Pulp 8 20 3 0.5 green_ton

price is currency per price_per measurement units. The shipped prices are illustrative and use United States dollars (USD).

product volume_unit price price_per
Large sawlog scribner 900 1000
Medium sawlog scribner 700 1000
Small sawlog scribner 500 1000
Pulp green_ton 30 1 
## Select logs from the tree
result <- optimize_bucking(dbh = tree$dbh,
                           ht = tree$ht,
                           model = tree$model,
                           species = tree$species,
                           id = tree$tree,
                           products = specifications,
                           currency = 'USD',
                           status = TRUE,
                           objective = 'value')
log product nominal_length sed_ib net_scale scale_unit
1 Large sawlog 32 14.017 230.000 board_foot
2 Medium sawlog 16 11.643 80.000 board_foot
3 Small sawlog 16 8.413 40.000 board_foot
4 Pulp 20 3.341 0.098 green_short_ton 
## Draw the optimized cuts
plot(result)

objective = 'auto' selects value when prices are present and net cubic volume otherwise. For value optimization, unpriced = 'zero' assigns zero value to unpriced products. unpriced = 'error' requires prices for every product.

Compare price scenarios

compare_bucking_prices() values existing cuts at each scenario’s prices, then optimizes the trees again. Every scenario must contain every product exactly once.

## Increase the example pulp price while retaining sawlog prices
scenarios <- specifications %>%
  transmute(scenario = 'higher_pulp',
            product,
            price = case_when(volume_unit == 'green_ton' ~ price * 2,
                              .default = price))
scenario product price
higher_pulp Large sawlog 900
higher_pulp Medium sawlog 700
higher_pulp Small sawlog 500
higher_pulp Pulp 60 
## Compare fixed cuts with cuts selected for the new prices
comparison <- compare_bucking_prices(x = result, price_scenarios = scenarios)
scenario currency repriced_value rebucked_value rebuck_gain
higher_pulp USD 288.903 288.903 0

repriced_value values the original cuts. rebucked_value values the newly selected cuts. rebuck_gain is their difference. Comparisons use unexpanded totals in each scenario’s currency.

The rebucked_results attribute retains each new result. Compare prices before applying later percentage deductions. Local models must remain registered for the repeated calculations.
